Track each endpoint by its eigenvalue spectrum of the Gram matrix, sorted slack profile, and contact-graph degree sequence, maintain a diverse elite pool of at least ten structurally distinct endpoints within $0.002$ of the best score, and only then apply intensive LP polishing across the pool; this tests whether the true optimum descends from a more rigid neighbouring code instead of the current single-contact basin.

direction: Perform coordinated rattler surgery to change the contact topology: freeze 51-63 points, choose the movable set jointly as the current maximising pair plus 6-18 rattlers whose row-max is closest to the global max or whose removal most reduces the near-contact band, and re-optimise that whole subset simultaneously against the frozen points and each other using multi-start Adam/CMA-style random tangent proposals with the true max objective, rather than deleting and refilling one point into the single farthest hole. Include moves that relocate a chosen rattler to a farthest hole of the configuration with itself removed, move a close pair apart symmetrically along their tangent bisector, and swap the positions of a high-load and a low-load point; accept moves by exact score after a short wide-band LP, and keep a tabu/archive list keyed by sorted pairwise-cosine fingerprints so the search is forced into subsets and topologies not recently visited.

Treat the ~435-pair plateau as the active set and alternate epsilon-scheduled trust-region LP with exact line search and kicks along the rigidity Jacobian null/soft directions accepted lexicographically on the top-50 sorted cosines.
direction: Build a rigidity-aware epsilon-active SQP/LP polisher that treats the plateau, not the single 1e-9 contact, as active: successively form pair sets with slack <1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6, 5e-8, build the tangent-space rigidity Jacobian for those pairs (project each pair gradient orthogonal to its two points, remove global SO(12) rotations), run trust-region LP minimising t on that set with exact-max line search, and intersperse random kicks restricted to the Jacobian's smallest-singular-value/null directions (which move the max pair apart almost for free) followed by re-polishing; report contacts at 5e-8 and the rigidity rank/singular spectrum, and keep a move only if the sorted top-50 cosine vector improves lexicographically, aiming to convert ~435 near-contacts into a genuinely rank-~715 jammed contact graph rather than repeatedly minimising one pair.

Leave-k-out global hole reinsertion targeting rattlers with massive uniform plus antipodal candidate pools refined by log-sum-exp spherical gradient descent and greedy sequential k=2,3 rebuilds with smooth quench acceptance.
direction: Exploit the rattlers by exact leave-$k$-out global reinsertion: rank points by (a) their largest cosine and (b) number of pairs within $10^{-3}$ of the max, then for the 10–20 loosest points, freeze the rest and globally relocate one point at a time — generate $\sim$20,000 candidates (uniform sphere, antipodes/negative combinations of frozen points, best points of a Fibonacci-type sample refined by local minimisation of $\max_j\langle y,x_j\rangle$ via log-sum-exp L-BFGS on the sphere), insert the best candidate, and repeat in cycles. Extend to $k=2,3$ simultaneous deletions with greedy sequential reinsertion and a short smooth quench (not LP) after each accepted move; accept only if the true 71-point max drops, otherwise restore. This targets precisely the 69 unconstrained points that coupled LP moves can only shift infinitesimally.

idea: Equalise the epsilon-plateau with exact active-set Gauss-Newton: QR-selected tight pairs solved as nonlinear dot=t equations by anchored Levenberg-Marquardt in tangent coordinates.
direction: Replace LP polishing with exact active-set Gauss-Newton equalisation: load `best.npy`, build the tangent Jacobian (781 coordinates) for pairs within $10^{-4}$ of the max, use pivoted QR on its rows to select a well-conditioned subset of $\sim$700 pairs, then solve the nonlinear square-ish system $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t=0$ for the selected pairs plus anchoring regularisation by Levenberg-Marquardt (`scipy.optimize.least_squares`, retraction by row normalisation, tangent variables via per-point SVD bases, residual scaling $10^{6}$). Re-select the active set and re-solve 3–5 times, accepting only true-max improvements; this directly tries to convert the fuzzy plateau into many machine-precision contacts rather than minimising a linearised upper bound. Keep the LP code out, cap each least-squares call (e.g. 25 s, `xtol/ftol=1e-14`), and return the best iterate before 170 s.

idea: Basin hopping with cheap annealed LogSumExp Adam quenches and three large topology moves with simulated-annealing acceptance on the top-20 vector.
direction: Do genuine basin hopping with uphill moves and a cheap smooth surrogate instead of one long LP run: run many short quenches minimising $\sum_{i<j}\exp((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-c_0)/T)$ or a $p$-norm ($p:32\to256$) objective with Adam/L-BFGS in pure NumPy, interleaved with large topology-changing perturbations — resample 5–20 loosest points, rotate a nearest-neighbour cluster of 5–15 points by 0.05–0.3 rad about a random axis in a random coordinate 2-plane, or swap a cluster toward the largest PCA gap. Accept perturbed quenches by simulated annealing on the lexicographic top-20 cosine vector allowing temporary worsening up to $10^{-4}$, keep an archive of distinct basins (separated by sorted-Gram fingerprints), and spend at most ~5–10 s per quench with time checks every iteration so dozens of basins are tried within the limit; return the best true configuration ever seen, falling back to `best.npy`.

idea: Leave-k-out global hole reinsertion targeting rattlers and hubs with massive candidate search plus log-sum-exp refinement and smooth quench acceptance.
direction: Exploit the rattlers by exact leave-$k$-out global reinsertion: rank points by (a) their largest cosine and (b) number of pairs within $10^{-3}$ of the max, then for the 10–20 loosest points, freeze the rest and globally relocate one point at a time — generate $\sim$20,000 candidates (uniform sphere, antipodes/negative combinations of frozen points, best points of a Fibonacci-type sample refined by local minimisation of $\max_j\langle y,x_j\rangle$ via log-sum-exp L-BFGS on the sphere), insert the best candidate, and repeat in cycles. Extend to $k=2,3$ simultaneous deletions with greedy sequential reinsertion and a short smooth quench (not LP) after each accepted move; accept only if the true 71-point max drops, otherwise restore. This targets precisely the 69 unconstrained points that coupled LP moves can only shift infinitesimally.

idea: Active-set Gauss-Newton equalisation of the epsilon-plateau into exact contacts via pivoted-QR selection and Levenberg-Marquardt on tangent coordinates.
direction: Replace LP polishing with exact active-set Gauss-Newton equalisation: load `best.npy`, build the tangent Jacobian (781 coordinates) for pairs within $10^{-4}$ of the max, use pivoted QR on its rows to select a well-conditioned subset of $\sim$700 pairs, then solve the nonlinear square-ish system $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t=0$ for the selected pairs plus anchoring regularisation by Levenberg-Marquardt (`scipy.optimize.least_squares`, retraction by row normalisation, tangent variables via per-point SVD bases, residual scaling $10^{6}$). Re-select the active set and re-solve 3–5 times, accepting only true-max improvements; this directly tries to convert the fuzzy plateau into many machine-precision contacts rather than minimising a linearised upper bound. Keep the LP code out, cap each least-squares call (e.g. 25 s, `xtol/ftol=1e-14`), and return the best iterate before 170 s.

idea: Multi-basin softmax-repulsion quench from random, D12-shell greedy and perturbed-record seeds combined with hole-reinsertion and hub-shake basin hopping plus final trust-region LP polish to leave the loose epsilon-plateau basin.

Search highly-symmetric single-orbit cyclic codes under C71 whose Gram depends only on six plane-weights via a tiny linear program, then break symmetry with annealed soft-max quenching and trust-region LP to land in a jammed basin with many exact contacts.

Defect-driven basin hopping from clean-slate LSE quenches — repeatedly delete worst points and reinsert into best holes plus targeted kicks to escape the single-contact epsilon-plateau, then low-temperature best-tracking polish.
